					<p style="text-align: center;"><em><strong>Salmon Rice Bowls</strong> – A layered bowl made up of tender jasmine rice, glazed teriyaki-style salmon bites, Asian cabbage slaw, fresh creamy avocado, and crisp cucumber. Then for a final finishing touch everything is drizzled with a spicy sriracha mayo. It’s a flavor explosion all in one spicy salmon rice bowl recipe!</em></p>

<h2 style="text-align: center;">Loaded Spicy Salmon Bowls</h2>
<p>These salmon rice bowls are loaded with the works! It’s an abundance of fresh ingredients all piled together in one bowl for maximum flavor.</p>
<p>You get a harmonious blend of various textures, an exciting combination of flavors that all highlight each other perfectly, and there’s a visually pleasing variety of vibrant colors.</p>
<p>It’s made up of nutritious ingredients and it’s such a filling dish. I’m a white rice fan lately but you can easily swap white jasmine rice for brown rice (regular, short grain, or jasmine brown rice) or quinoa.</p>
<p>I’ve also listed other various substitutes to use in this dish based on what you have on hand (see ideas below).</p>
<p>This is one to add to the dinner rotation, it’s incredibly delicious!</p>

<h2>Salmon Rice Bowl Recipe Ingredients</h2>
<ul>
<li>Vegetables:<strong> coleslaw mix, green onions, ginger, garlic, avocado, cucumber</strong></li>
<li>Seasonings: <strong>soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sriracha, mirin, honey, salt and black pepper</strong></li>
<li>Thickener: <strong>cornstarch</strong></li>
<li>Base ingredients: <strong>salmon, jasmine rice, sesame seeds</strong></li>
<li>Fats: <strong>mayonnaise, olive oil</strong></li>
</ul>

<h2>How to Make Salmon Rice Bowls</h2>
<ol>
<li><strong>Cook rice</strong> according to directions on package.</li>
<li><strong>Mix sriracha mayo:</strong> Mix together mayonnaise and sriracha in a small bowl. Transfer to a small resealable bag.</li>
<li><strong>Make the slaw:</strong> In a large mixing bowl toss together coleslaw mix, green onions, rice vinegar, 1 Tbsp honey, 1 tsp soy sauce and 1/2 tsp sesame oil. Season lightly with salt to taste. Set mixture aside.</li>
<li><strong>Make the salmon sauce:</strong> In a small mixing bowl whisk together remaining 3 Tbsp soy sauce, 2 Tbsp mirin, 1 Tbsp honey, 1/2 tsp sesame oil, the ginger, garlic and cornstarch until mixture is well blended (cornstarch should be dissolved). Set aside.</li>
<li><strong>Cook salmon:</strong> After cutting fillets, dab salmon pieces dry with paper towels, season with pepper only. Preheat a 12-inch non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Add olive oil.</li>
<li>Quickly spread salmon pieces out evenly in skillet pan. Let sear on one side only until salmon is nearly cooked, about 2 to 3 minutes.</li>
<li><strong>Add sauce:</strong> Whisk cornstarch mixture once more then pour over salmon. Cook, gently tossing for about 20 to 30 seconds until the mixture is thickened.</li>
<li><strong>Assemble bowls:</strong> Layer cooked rice into serving bowls. In sections top with salmon, the slaw veggies , avocado, and cucumber. Sprinkle over sesame seeds then cut corner from spicy mayo bag and drizzle over.</li>
</ol>

<h2>Possible Variations on this Spicy Salmon Bowl Recipe</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>White rice substitute:</strong> Brown rice, cauliflower rice, quinoa, or farro would work well in place of white sushi rice.</li>
<li><strong>Make your own coleslaw mix:</strong> Rather than using a store-bought coleslaw mix you can use 2 cups thinly sliced green cabbage, 1 1/2 cups thinly sliced red cabbage, and 1/2 cup carrots cut into matchsticks.</li>
<li><strong>Mirin substitute:</strong> Dry sherry would work in a pinch.</li>
<li><strong>Rice vinegar alternative:</strong> Apple cider vinegar is another great choice.</li>
<li><strong>Less sodium option:</strong> If you want to cut sodium use low-sodium soy sauce or tamari, don’t add additional salt to the recipe.</li>
<li><strong>Honey alternative: </strong>Real maple syrup or brown sugar will work in place of honey.</li>
<li><strong>Healthier mayo option:</strong> Plain Greek yogurt can be used in place of mayo to make it healthier. Or you can use light mayo.</li>
<li><strong>Use other vegetables:</strong> So many options on this one. You could use other vegetables like bok choy, spinach, broccoli slaw, bell pepper, snap peas, sauteed mushrooms etc.</li>
<li><strong>Chicken for salmon:</strong> Chopped chicken breasts can be used in place of salmon, just cook through completely (it will take about 6 minutes to cook).</li>
</ul>

<h2>Make Ahead Meal Prep</h2>
<ul>
<li>Salmon and rice can be prepared a day in advance, store in the fridge (preferably not layered or salmon marinade will soak into salmon).</li>
<li>Reheat in the microwave on 50% power until heated through.</li>
<li>Slaw can be prepared a day ahead and cucumber can be sliced ahead, just wait to add to heated bowl.</li>
<li>Chop avocado just before serving.</li>
</ul>
